title: Hess’s law and standard formation enthalpy
objective: Combine thermochemical equations, identify formation reactions, and calculate standard reaction enthalpy.

items: Reaction enthalpies add when their equations add.
Enthalpy to form one mole from elements in their reference states.

blocks.title: Common errors
blocks.md: Reverse the sign only when reversing an equation. Phases matter. Zero applies to an element in its reference state.

blocks.title: Exam practice
blocks.md: For a formation equation, check the product coefficient and the physical forms of the elements. For a table calculation, check the order of subtraction.

blocks.title: Hess’s law and enthalpy changes
blocks.focus: Annotate each reversal and scaling factor before canceling species.

blocks.title: Subtract one pathway
blocks.problem: Given $\ce{C(graphite) + O2(g) -> CO2(g)}$, $-393.5$ kJ, and $\ce{CO(g) + 1/2 O2(g) -> CO2(g)}$, $-283.0$ kJ, find $\Delta H$ for $\ce{C(graphite) + 1/2 O2(g) -> CO(g)}$.

steps.title: Place CO on the product side
steps.md: Reverse the second equation and use $+283.0$ kJ.

steps.title: Cancel
steps.md: Cancel carbon dioxide and half of the oxygen. Add $-393.5+283.0$.
steps.why: The sum must reproduce the target equation.

blocks.title: Use formation data
blocks.problem: For $\ce{CaCO3(s) -> CaO(s) + CO2(g)}$, use formation enthalpies $-1207$, $-635$, and $-394$ kJ/mol respectively.
